hook: The shopkeeper charged me more than the MRP.

slides.title: No. MRP is the maximum.
slides.body: The retail sale price printed on a packaged product is the maximum price at which it may be sold to you.

slides.title: Taxes are already included.
slides.body: The printed price is inclusive of all taxes, so a seller can't add GST or any other tax on top of it.

slides.title: Selling above MRP is not allowed.
slides.body: No retailer, wholesaler, manufacturer or anyone else may sell a packaged product for more than its retail sale price.

slides.title: Every retail package must show it.
slides.body: Pre-packed products for retail sale must declare the MRP in rupees, inclusive of all taxes. A few packs are exempt, like those over 25 kg or 25 litres, or goods for industrial buyers.
slides.ref: Packaged Commodities Rules 2011 · Rules 3, 6 · PIB, Nov 2021

slides.title: How to complain:
list: Call the National Consumer Helpline: 1915 or 1800-11-4000 (8 AM to 8 PM)
File online at consumerhelpline.gov.in or on the NCH app

sources: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 – Rules 2, 3, 6, 18 (as amended)
PIB, Department of Consumer Affairs, Nov 2021: MRP inclusive of all taxes
caption:
Charged more than the MRP? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ The MRP is the maximum price a packaged product can be sold for
2️⃣ It already includes all taxes, so no GST can be added on top
3️⃣ No seller may charge more than the printed retail sale price
4️⃣ Complain to the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915, or WhatsApp/SMS 8800001915

Source: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011; PIB (Nov 2021); consumerhelpline.gov.in
